rationale: Three layers, one rule: keep what cannot be recreated, regenerate what can. The raw downloads and the uniform per-country files are irreplaceable and currently have no durability at all — they live outside any git repository, unhashed and unbacked. The per-municipality fan-out and the generated pages are build output: reproducible from the uniform layer, so they are regenerated into the serving snapshot rather than committed. The manifest this config produces stays in git, which is what keeps the whole chain auditable after the fan-out stops being committed.

layers.title: Original downloads, exactly as fetched
layers.recreatable: only by refetching national sources, several of which are not stable: Costa Rica is a portal query, Spain publishes year-stamped archives that are replaced in place

layers.title: One normalised file per country
layers.recreatable: from raw, by rerunning the country extractors

layers.title: Per-municipality fan-out
layers.recreatable: for twelve countries, from the warehouse plus the entity directory and headline rules, verified on every published headline — 51,020 checks, all agreeing
layers.note: Twelve of the fifteen countries are now built from the warehouse rather than read from here: prepare-public-serving-snapshots.mjs prefers .warehouse-profiles/<country> whenever that country's headline rules reproduce every published figure and its profiles have been built, and falls back to these files otherwise. Brazil, Denmark and Japan still come from here. Note this is not a size saving — the warehouse build is larger, 160.5 MB against 146.3 MB for the same twelve, because the fan-out was lossy and Spain alone gains 14% of rows back. What changes is that those profiles become derived rather than stored, so they no longer need hydrating and verifying as a data layer.

layers.title: Generated municipal profile pages
layers.recreatable: from the uniform layer via scripts/build-municipal-expansion-pages.py and scripts/build-municipality-country-pages.mjs; run-to-run output verified byte-identical
layers.note: 29,597 files. Every regeneration rewrote all of them into history. Prerendered HTML is correct for SEO and no-JS readers; committing it is what was wrong.

layers.title: Generated Czech municipal pages
layers.recreatable: from pipeline/transforms/build_czech_site.py, the single source of every page under cz/

layers.title: Per-entity machine-readable profiles
layers.recreatable: from pipeline/transforms/build_municipal_public_site.py, which rebuilds the directory from scratch; verified byte-identical across 6,267 files. Inputs are data/municipal-snapshot.v1.json, data/benchmark.v1.json and data/large-city-history.v1.json, all committed.
layers.note: 6,254 municipalities are a verbatim fan-out of municipal-snapshot — every field reproduces from it exactly — plus the 13 Czech regions, which come from benchmark.v1.json.

layers.title: Municipal entity directory
layers.recreatable: from the serving fan-out today; from the warehouse plus each national source's own name column once the snapshot generator is rewired
layers.note: Entity identity extracted from the fan-out: name, region, population, currency, reporting basis and page URL for 28,559 municipalities across 15 countries, 4.6 MB against the fan-out's 580 MB. This is the layer whose absence kept the fan-out alive. The warehouse holds every fact those files carry — verified for BR:1100015, where actual/TotalReceitas reproduces the published 147,350,577.63 to the cent — but it does not know that CR:SIPP-ABANGARES is Abangares. Small enough to commit, so it is committed.

known_gaps.detail: The committed pages are stale relative to their template: regenerating applies the copy-voice rewrite they never received, and a sort-order and numeric-type normalisation in international-municipalities.v1.json. Refreshing that baseline is a separate reviewable change from un-committing, and is deliberately not bundled here.

Brazil's extractor mislabels budget_side on 454,916 rows. 101 revenue codes — ReceitaTributaria, Impostos, Taxas, TransferenciasCorrentes among them — arrive marked `expenditure` across all 5,570 municipalities, and none ever arrives marked `revenue`. The RREO column heading is authoritative (revenue uses PREVISÃO / No Bimestre / Até o Bimestre; expenditure uses DOTAÇÃO / DESPESAS), so the warehouse loader corrects from it and flags each corrected row side_corrected_from_source_column. The uniform layer and the committed per-municipality files still carry the defect, so the live site shows it until the extractor is fixed upstream or the fan-out is regenerated from a corrected view. Detectable only because Brazil publishes column labels; the other countries carry none, though their revenue-to-expenditure balances are all plausible.

The fan-out is stale where the warehouse is corrected. For BR:1100015 only 69 of 239 fan-out detail rows survive as-is: the files predate the budget_side repair and carry a different stage vocabulary (`cash`, `execution`) than the loaded lifecycle (`enacted → revised → committed → actual → paid`). The headline reconciles exactly, so the published figures are not at risk, but the two are not interchangeable and the fan-out is the wrong one. Retiring it needs prepare-public-serving-snapshots.mjs to build profiles from the warehouse and the entity directory rather than from these files.

Japan is the only country whose facts the warehouse cannot supply, so data/municipal-expansion/jpn (110.9 MB, 1,741 entities) must stay until the e-Stat hierarchy is settled. Its identity is already extracted, so the other fourteen countries are no longer waiting on it.

Profiles now build from the warehouse (scripts/build-profiles-from-warehouse.mjs), and the headline they lead with was checked against every entity the site publishes, not a sample. Twelve countries agree exactly: Costa Rica 168/168, Georgia 276/276, El Salvador 518/518, Korea 486/486, Bolivia 686/686, Chile 690/690, Guatemala 680/680, Colombia 2,204/2,204, Mexico 4,760/4,760, Peru 3,782/3,782, Italy 15,792/15,792, Spain 20,978/20,978. Brazil is 11,070 of 11,114.

The derived headline rules are only as good as the entities sampled, and an even spread hides a year a small minority uses: 44 of Brazil's 5,570 municipalities report 2024 rather than 2025, so a 40-entity sample contained none of them and no 2024 rule was derived at all. Sampling is now stratified by year. A related accounting flaw is fixed too — a year with no workable rule used to drop out of both the display and the coverage sum, so a country missing an entire year's rule still reported 100%.

Brazil's 2024 DCA is loaded and its profiles reproduce every published headline: 11,114 of 11,114 across all 5,570 municipalities, both years. The 11,864 second-hand rows that came through the RREO loader were replaced by 12,046 read from the raw annexes, and the column heading is now kept in source_budget_item_type_code with FUNDEB deductions marked is_consolidation_item. Headline queries exclude consolidation items, without which a gross revenue and the deduction taken from it sum back together — the defect that inflated BR:1302405 by 7,265,266.90.

Japan is still not loaded, but for a different reason than recorded before, and the earlier figures were measured on truncated input. The hierarchy is derivable without the e-Stat table definitions: scripts/derive-japan-hierarchy.mjs finds a parent by arithmetic — a column equal to the sum of the columns beneath it for every municipality — and collapses table 04's 69 revenue columns to 20 top-level ones, correctly recovering 地方譲与税 over its six transfer taxes and 地方交付税 over its three. What it then shows is that the cached extract is incomplete: those 20 columns come to a median 0.713 of the 歳入総額 that table 02 prints, so roughly 29% of revenue — local bonds, carryover, prefectural disbursements, miscellaneous — is in parts of 歳入内訳 that were never fetched. The earlier 2.47x was measured against the importer's output, which caps detail at 360 rows per municipality, so it mixed an over-count from the hierarchy with an under-count from truncation.

Denmark is re-extracted, loaded and serving. REGK100 across all seven dranst with ART=UE,I closes the accounts: Copenhagen 2025 is 68,818,554 thousand kroner out against 68,818,541 in, where the previous extract missed by 33,072,000. That extract was also wrong beyond the missing side — its dranst 1 operating expenditure was 31,850.3m against a true 55,925.2m. The 209,152 superseded regk31 rows were replaced by 70,145 from regk100; the budk32 enacted-budget rows were left alone, because REGK100 is the final accounts and replaces only the actual stage.

24 of Denmark's 196 entity-years do not balance in the source itself, by between 0.2% and 4.5% of expenditure, and one municipality reports negative gross expenditure — corrections flowing through a published series. The other 172 close to within rounding. This is recorded rather than absorbed into a tolerance: a threshold wide enough to swallow 4.5% would also swallow a real loading defect.

Denmark's headline rule is authored rather than derived, and the serving gate now distinguishes the two. A derived rule reproduces every figure the site already publishes; an authored one has no such check, so it is allowed only where the site publishes no headline at all and switching cannot regress one. Denmark qualifies on that basis, and its justification is recorded in municipal_headline_rules.json: the Danish account plan balances by construction, so a headline keeping financing in reports every municipality as revenue exactly equal to expenditure. Excluding financing — dranst 4, 5, 6 and borrowing under function 8.55 — gives Copenhagen 67.58bn against 67.12bn, a 0.46bn surplus, and across 196 entity-years the ratio runs 0.952 to 1.075 with 148 in surplus.

Japan's expenditure tables are now read correctly, and the earlier tenfold over-count was a misreading of what they are. Tables 07-12 are expenditure by purpose and their purposes are disjoint — 議会費 and 総務費 in 07, 民生費 and 衛生費 in 08, through to 災害復旧費, 公債費 and 諸支出金 in 12. Table 13 is not a seventh purpose table: it is 歳出合計 beside the funding sources that meet it (国庫支出金, 都道府県支出金, 使用料手数料, 分担金負担金寄附金, 財産収入, 繰入金, 諸収入, 繰越金, 地方債, 一般財源等). Summing it as though it were a purpose adds the whole budget a second time. The nature rows nest the same way the columns do — 人件費 over うち職員給, 補助費等 over rows 07-11, 普通建設事業費 over 13-17 — so the top level is rows 01, 03, 04, 05, 06, 12, 18 and 21.

Two things still block Japan, and neither is inference. First, 表05 収入の状況_1 was never fetched — statInfId 000040375639, now cached — and its 21 revenue categories run 地方税 through 財産収入, coming to 81.9% of Sapporo's published 歳入総額. The remainder (寄附金, 繰入金, 繰越金, 諸収入, 地方債) is in a 収入の状況_2 whose file id is not adjacent: 000040375637 and 000040375640 through 000040375642 all return 404, and e-Stat's file listing is rendered client-side with no statInfId in the markup, so finding it means driving the portal's dataset list rather than guessing ids. Second, a scope difference: table 13's 歳出合計 agrees exactly with its own funding-source total for every municipality, which says the table is coherent, but both come to only 78-80% of the 歳出総額 that table 02 prints. Something in the survey's account scope differs between those two tables and it has to be identified before either can be published as the other's breakdown.
